issues.description: Name mismatch for the screen buffer variable: the problem statement and the template define/use the symbol 'display_start' as the base address of the framebuffer, but the solution's .bss defines 'screen_buffer' while its code still references 'display_start'. This creates an undefined-symbol/namespace inconsistency (solution references a variable that is not defined) and will confuse students when comparing artifacts or when trying to assemble/run the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the framebuffer symbol name consistent across all artifacts. Either rename 'screen_buffer' in the solution .bss to 'display_start' or change all references to 'display_start' in the solution to 'screen_buffer'. Ensure the name matches the template and the problem statement so the symbol is defined and referenced consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template refer to the screen memory start as 'display_start', but the solution repository defines the same conceptual buffer as 'screen_buffer'. This inconsistent identifier naming for the same conceptual entity (the start of the screen/framebuffer) creates a mapping burden: students reading the solution to learn the intended implementation may not immediately realize 'screen_buffer' in the solution corresponds to 'display_start' used in the task text and template.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent identifier for the screen memory start across all artifacts. Prefer renaming the solution's 'screen_buffer' to 'display_start' (and update any references), or alternatively rename the template/problem occurrences to 'screen_buffer' so all three artifacts use the same name.
